input.quote: (b) Customer agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Kubient and its owners, shareholders, officers, directors, managers, agents, and employees from all third-party Claims arising out of or in connection with (i) Customer's unauthorized or inappropriate use of the Services, (ii) Customer's unauthorized or inappropriate use of the Auction Platform, (iii) Customer's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement, or (iv) the Content or Properties, including any allegation or claim that the Content or Properties violate or infringe on an y third party rig hts, or (v) the acts or omissions of Customer or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Customer's control.
input.rationale: Section 10(a) does contain a Kubient indemnity covering the Services, the Auction Platform and Kubient's breach of its warranties (which include IP ownership warranties at 9(b)(vii)-(viii)), and Section 11 sets out standard notice/control/cooperation procedures, so the vendor-side limb of the rule is largely met. Two deviations remain: (1) the Customer-side indemnity in 10(b) is far broader than the playbook's narrow position, extending to any breach of any representation or warranty and to an open-ended catch-all for the acts or omissions of Customer or anyone under its control; and (2) Kubient's indemnity for Creative served through its own Auction Platform is cut back by a "to the best of its knowledge" qualifier, weakening cover for third-party IP/content claims arising from demand Kubient controls. The redline narrows our indemnity to Content/Properties and our breach of applicable Law and deletes the knowledge qualifier.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have narrowed our indemnity to the Content and Properties we supply and our breach of applicable Law, deleting the open-ended catch-all for our acts or omissions and any breach of warranty, and removed the knowledge qualifier from Kubient's indemnity for Creative served through the Auction Platform so that third-party IP and content claims sit with the party controlling the demand source. Our position is that the customer-side indemnity stays narrow while the vendor indemnity covers IP infringement without a knowledge cut-back.
proposal.summary: Narrow Customer indemnity to Content/Properties and breach of Law; remove knowledge qualifier from Kubient's Creative indemnity.
